hero.title: 1. Why Choose Ireland to Study Biotechnology?
hero.subtitle: Biological science, pharmaceutical innovation, medical research and industrial biotechnology are all popular subjects for students in Ireland. The country boasts a significant biopharmaceutical and life-sciences sectorpresenting opportunities for graduates with relevant scientific and technical skills.

sections.title: Eligibility to Study Bio-Technology in Ireland
sections.lead: Eligibility requirements for biotechnology in Ireland differ based on whether you are applying for an undergraduate or postgraduate program.

items: Undergraduate Students of Biotechnology:
- Completion of Class 12 or an equivalent secondary school qualification.
- Academic grades required in science subjects.
- Knowledge of biology and chemistry, mathematics or other subjects required by some institutions.
- English Language Skills.
- Further specifications required by the university.
Universities assess Class 12 qualifications of Indian students on a case-to-case basis.
For postgraduate biotechnology:
- A recognized bachelor's degree in biotechnology, microbiology, biochemistry, biology, biomedical science, chemistry or other recognized fields.
- Minimum grade or equivalent required by the university.
- Scientific knowledge relevant to the program and, in some programs, laboratory or research experience.
- Ability to speak English.

sections.title: Ireland Biotechnology Admission Requirements
sections.lead: The biotechnology course entry requirements in Ireland are normally based on your academic performance, subject preparation and your English language proficiency.

items: Academic requirements: Secondary-school entry criteria apply to undergraduate applicants.

English language requirements: IELTS Academic, TOEFL or other approved tests may be accepted.

faqs.q: How long does it take to study biotechnology in Ireland?
faqs.a: The standard period of a BSc in Biotechnology is four years. Full-time master's programs are often one year long, though the exact duration can differ between institutions and course design.

faqs.q: Can Indian students do biotechnology after 12th in Ireland?
faqs.a: Yes. You need to meet the university's academic, science subject, English language and other entry requirements. Universities assess Indian qualifications on a case-by-case basis.

faqs.q: How much is tuition for biotechnology in Ireland?
faqs.a: For non-EU students undergraduate programs can cost around €13,500–€30,000 a year. A one-year masters can be around €27,000-€30,000, perhaps with extra lab fees.

faqs.q: Is biotechnology done? Can I get a job in Ireland?
faqs.a: Graduates can apply for suitable positions in laboratory research, biopharmaceutical manufacturing, quality control, quality assurance and related areas. The employment depends on the available vacancies, skills, qualifications and the applicable work permission for the graduate.

faqs.q: Is biotechnology a good choice for international students in Ireland?
faqs.a: It can accommodate students interested in life sciences, laboratory work, pharmaceutical manufacturing and research. Before choosing a program, compare the tuition, laboratory training, industry links, living costs and relevance to your career.
